 Epictetus. (c.A.D. 50–c.A.D. 138).  The Golden Sayings of Epictetus.
The Harvard Classics.  1909–14.

LXIX

I think I know now what I never knew before—the meaning of the common saying, 
A fool you can neither bend nor break.
 Pray heaven I may never have a 
wise fool
 for my friend! There is nothing more intractable.—“My resolve is fixed!”—Why, so madmen say too; but the more firmly they believe in their delusions, the more they stand in need of treatment.
